$comment: Test files are excluded from the package builds so they never reach dist, which is correct - shipping compiled tests would be wrong. But it also means `tsc -b` never sees them, and v2's `typecheck` was only `tsc -b`, so NO v2 test file was type-checked at all. A test can therefore hold a type error that surfaces only when it runs, or worse, hold a type that silently collapses to `never` and checks nothing: ai-provider.test.ts typed its mock response through `Parameters<Parameters<typeof createServer>[0]>[1]`, which picked the wrong overload, became `never`, and made the file's assertions vacuous - inside the test file for CS-48, whose AC7 was itself about a test that could not fail. This project checks those files with no emit, mirroring the root workspace's tsconfig.test.json, which has solved the same problem for the root packages since it was added. NOTE ON apps/workers: it is absent from `include` below, deliberately - its own test files have known issues and ownership of that path is unconfirmed, so enumerating them here would be reaching into someone else's work. That is a scoping decision about the include LIST, not a claim that the directory is unchecked: files under apps/workers are pulled in as dependencies of included files (verified - apps/workers/search/src/collect.ts appears in the resolved file set), so type errors there are reported. 'Not enumerated' and 'not checked' are different things.
$lib-comment: `lib: ES2024` is a correction, not an accommodation. v2/tsconfig.base.json sets `target: ES2023` with no explicit lib, so the default lib denies Promise.withResolvers - an ES2024 API. But this project requires Node >=24 in six places, deploys on Node 24, and Node 24 provides it (verified: `typeof Promise.withResolvers === 'function'` on node:24.21.0). The declaration understated its own runtime by a year. It is also NOT confined to tests: v2/scripts/check-ui.ts, the V2 browser acceptance suite, uses it too - and compiled only because v2/scripts was in no tsconfig at all. Setting it here fixes the checking project without changing emit for any consumer; v2/tsconfig.base.json should follow, but that file is outside this session's ownership so the change is recorded rather than made.
$paths-comment: v2/packages/core/package.json has no `types` and no `main`, only an `exports` map pointing at dist. So a test importing `@careerscope/core` resolved its declarations from dist/ while importing a sibling by relative path resolved from src/, and TypeScript treated the two declaration files as nominally distinct types - 40 of the original 96 diagnostics. RECORDED CAVEAT, because this mapping is not free: the split is NOT purely a type artifact. At runtime `tsx` honours the exports map, so the package's Database and src's Database are genuinely different classes - verified by probe: identity false, package resolves to dist/index.js, and a dist instance is not instanceof the src class. This mapping tells the compiler they are one thing. That is right for type-checking a test against the source it exercises, but the compiler no longer flags the real cross-instance boundary, notably database.test.ts:1617/1620, which compares ResumeConflict (src) against Conflict (dist) deliberately. That boundary now rests on its runtime assertion alone.
